alertSettings.title: Alert settings
alertSettings.notSaved: Nothing saved yet, so the reporter uses its REPORT_ALERTS environment settings. The form shows the built-in defaults until you save.
alertSettings.thresholdsHint: Alert once per week when a Claude account's weekly limit passes each percent (default 80 and 90).

pace.label: Pace
pace.desc: Warn when an account is on pace to run out before the weekly reset.

summary.label: Weekly summary
summary.desc: Post the report image with a recap in the last hour before the weekly reset.

stale.label: Stale app
stale.desc: Warn when an active member's app has not synced for 24 hours.

runaway.label: Runaway session
runaway.desc: Warn when one session uses the runaway share of its weekly limit within an hour.

project.label: Project share
project.desc: Warn when one project passes the project share of the team's weekly tokens.

budget.label: Fair share
budget.desc: Warn when a member of a shared account uses more than their fair share of the day.

version.label: App version
version.desc: Warn when a member runs an older app than the newest one on the team.

alertSettings.runawayShareHint: Percent of the weekly limit one session may use within an hour (default 5).
alertSettings.projectShareHint: Percent of the team's weekly tokens one project may use (default 40).
alertSettings.invalidShare: Enter a whole number from 1 to 100.

planUsage.title: Plan usage, last 7 days
planUsage.empty: No usage in the last 7 days.
planUsage.footnote: In includes cache read and write. Share weighs output 5×. Cost is the 7-day limit used times the weekly plan allowance, estimated from the plan tier. Members on the same Claude account split its cost by share each day. An amber outline marks a day above the member's fair share of the 14.3%/day pace (split between members of the account).

weeks.note: Each row is one Claude 7-day limit window with the last reading of that window. Cost is the limit used times the weekly plan allowance; members split it by token share (input including cache, output counts 5×).
